blocks.content: A Job's behavior is tuned by a small set of fields, how many successful completions it needs, how many Pods run at once, how many retries it allows, and an overall time limit, this topic covers each one precisely.

completions sets the total number of successful Pod completions the Job needs before it considers itself done, by default this is 1, a single successful run, but it can be set higher for work meant to run several times.

blocks.alt: The total number of successes needed before the Job is considered finished

blocks.content: 2. parallelism: How Many Run at Once
blocks.text: 2. parallelism: How Many Run at Once

blocks.content: parallelism controls how many Pods run concurrently while working toward that completion goal, covered in full mechanical detail in the next topic, Parallel Jobs.

blocks.alt: How many Pods are actively working at the same time, covered fully next

blocks.content: As introduced in the Job topic, failed Pods are retried, backoffLimit caps exactly how many retries are allowed before the Job gives up entirely and marks itself as failed, rather than retrying forever.

blocks.alt: A real ceiling on retries, the Job does not retry indefinitely

blocks.content:
spec:
  backoffLimit: 4   # give up after 4 failed attempts

code.content:
spec:
  backoffLimit: 4   # give up after 4 failed attempts

codes.yaml:
spec:
  backoffLimit: 4   # give up after 4 failed attempts

blocks.content: Beyond capping retry count, activeDeadlineSeconds caps the Job's total wall-clock runtime, if the Job (across all its Pods and retries) has not finished within this window, it is terminated regardless of how many retries remain.

blocks.alt: A hard overall time limit, independent of the retry count itself

blocks.content: A realistic Job manifest often sets several of these together, a completion target, a reasonable parallelism, a sensible retry limit, and an overall deadline, giving the Job well-defined, bounded behavior in every dimension.

blocks.alt: Every dimension bounded deliberately, not left to defaults by accident

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: completions sets the total success goal, parallelism controls concurrency, backoffLimit caps retries, and activeDeadlineSeconds caps overall runtime.
Together, these four fields give a Job well-defined, bounded behavior in every dimension, worth setting deliberately rather than relying on defaults.
